title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-18
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard transfer captures a jazzy 1973 Tampa show highlighted by an epic Weather Report Suite → Dark Star sequence and crystal‑clear instrumentation.
ai_review.review: The Miller remaster of the December 18, 1973 Tampa concert delivers breathtaking clarity—every bass note, piano chord, and Jerry Garcia solo rings out with pristine detail. Musically the night shines thanks to a soaring Weather Report Suite into Dark Star, flawless Eyes of the World, and a soulful Wharf Rat, all linked by seamless transitions that showcase the band at peak improvisational form.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 five‑star reviews uniformly praise both the sound quality and performance; minor critiques are limited to vocal distance or tiny patch artifacts, yielding an overall rating near the top of the scale.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remastered by Charlie Miller; reviewers describe the sound as crisp, brilliant, with superb low‑end definition and vivid instrument separation. A few note a tiny AUD patch in the outro but it does not detract from overall fidelity.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Transitions are highlighted as seamless—especially WRS → Dark Star → Drums → Eyes → Wharf Rat and the China‑Rider segue—creating a jazzy, flowing second set that builds tension and releases it beautifully.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for his soaring solo work, slide‑like tone on Dark Star and WRS, and overall confident, ‘captain trips’ performance.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for prominent, crunchy bass that drives the jams; noted for jazzy counterpoint especially in WRS and Eyes of the World.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is highlighted as front‑and‑center in the mix with lush piano/organ work on WRS, GSET, and throughout the set; his playing described as 'subtle genius' and a key part of the jazzy feel.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming called solid, steady, and integral to the transitions, especially during the Drum solo leading into Eyes.
